name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
principle: User-controllable input is placed into a generated web page without context-appropriate neutralization. A browser may interpret the data as HTML, JavaScript, CSS, or URL code and execute attacker-controlled actions in the victim's session.
detection_signals: Java Servlet/JSP: request.getParameter(...), request.getHeader(...), or Cookie.getValue() concatenated into out.print(...), response.getWriter().write(...), or <%= ... %>
Stored XSS: ResultSet.getString(...), ORM entity field, file data, or message text written to an HTML response without Encode.forHtml(...) or template auto-escape
DOM XSS: location, document.URL, document.referrer, window.name, or postMessage data assigned to innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, or document.write(...)
HTML attribute sink: user data concatenated into href=, src=, value=, title=, style=, or on* attributes without Encode.forHtmlAttribute(...)
JavaScript sink: user data embedded in <script>, event handler, eval(...), setTimeout(string), setInterval(string), or Function(...) without JavaScript-string encoding
URL sink: user data concatenated into href, src, action, or redirect URL with javascript: allowed or without URL allowlist plus Encode.forUriComponent(...)
C/C++ CGI: getenv("QUERY_STRING"), POST body, socket input, or parsed parameter passed to printf("<html>...%s", value) without HTML encoding
negative_signals: Output uses context-specific encoder matching the sink: Encode.forHtml, Encode.forHtmlAttribute, Encode.forJavaScript, Encode.forCssString, Encode.forUriComponent, or ESAPI.encoder()
Template auto-escaping is enabled for the context, e.g. JSP c:out escapeXml=true, Thymeleaf th:text, React JSX text interpolation, or Angular interpolation
Value is a compile-time constant, enum-only value, or server-generated token with no request, cookie, header, file, database, or network influence
HTML attribute value is quoted and encoded with an attribute encoder before output
Untrusted rich HTML is sanitized by an allowlist sanitizer such as OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer or DOMPurify before insertion
Response specifies a consistent charset, e.g. Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8, and output encoding is applied before writing
false_defense_traps: Blacklist removal of "script" misses mixed case, encoded input, SVG, IMG onerror, and event-handler payloads
HTML body escaping used inside JavaScript, CSS, URL, or attribute contexts is the wrong encoder
SQL escaping, prepared statements, or mysql_real_escape_string protect SQL only; stored HTML can still execute when rendered
Client-side validation or JavaScript filtering only is bypassable by modified requests
HttpOnly cookies, SameSite cookies, and CSP reduce impact but do not neutralize injected page content
verification_focus: Does any attacker-influenced value reach an HTML, attribute, URL, JavaScript, CSS, or DOM output sink without the encoder or sanitizer required for that exact context?

consequence_chains.trigger: Missing or wrong output encoding before web page generation
consequence_chains.consequence: Browser executes attacker-controlled script or markup

consequence_chains.trigger: Incomplete blacklist filter is bypassed with alternate XSS syntax
consequence_chains.consequence: Injected script steals data or modifies page actions

consequence_chains.trigger: SQL injection stores malicious HTML that is later rendered to users
consequence_chains.consequence: Second-order stored XSS and account compromise

consequence_chains.trigger: Injected script issues authenticated same-origin requests
consequence_chains.consequence: Victim actions are forged using the active session

patch_principle: Encode on output using the exact encoder for the context: HTML body, HTML attribute, URL component, JavaScript string, or CSS.
Prefer vetted frameworks and template engines with context-aware auto-escaping enabled.
Sanitize user-supplied rich HTML with an allowlist sanitizer; otherwise render it as plain text.
Validate input with accept-known-good rules, but still apply output encoding.
Add defense in depth with HttpOnly and SameSite cookies, CSP, and explicit UTF-8 charset.
